title: Closed extraordinary restriction commutes with finite direct image
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $p:X'\to X$ be a finite morphism of Noetherian schemes (schemes admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings) and $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Form $Y'=Y\times_X X'$ with projections $i':Y'\hookrightarrow X'$ and $p':Y'\to Y$, and put $q=pi'=ip'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. On ordinary small-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], use the bounded-below right adjoints $i^!,i'^!$ to exact closed direct image, and exact finite direct images $p_*,p'_*,q_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, lem-exc-closed-ambient]. There is a natural isomorphism
$$i^!p_*M\cong p'_*i'^!M\qquad(M\in D^+(X'_{\mathrm{et}},A)).$$
Under $i^!i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ and this isomorphism, the map
$$i^!\bigl(p_*i'_*i'^!M\longrightarrow p_*M\bigr)$$
obtained from the counit for $i'$ is the identity of $p'_*i'^!M$. In particular it is an isomorphism. The exchange uses the canonical pullback/closed-direct-image base-change map and the ordinary adjunctions; the displayed normalization fixes the counit map, rather than merely asserting that its source and target are isomorphic.

proof.text: The base change $i'$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Finiteness of $p'$ can also be checked directly: over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$ write $X'=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ generated over $R$ by $b_1,\ldots,b_r$, and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$. Then $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}(B/IB)$ and the images of the same $b_a$ generate over $R/I$. This is precisely [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The maps $i,i'$ are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], and $q=pi'=ip'$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. The direct-image formula of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], evaluated on an etale $V\to X$, identifies both $p_*i'_*N$ and $i_*p'_*N$ with $N(V\times_XY')$. Denote this canonical identification by $c_N:i_*p'_*N\xrightarrow{\sim}p_*i'_*N$.

source.place: Stacks Tags 01QR, 035C, 01WK; finite base change on affine charts; direct image evaluated on fibre products

proof.text: By [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] the direct images of all five finite maps are exact on abelian sheaves. This gives exactness on $A$-module sheaves as well: by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] kernels are computed sectionwise and cokernels by sheafifying the sectionwise cokernels, so forgetting the action preserves and detects exactness. The direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] commutes with this forgetting. Likewise inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], with the same conclusion for the induced constant-coefficient module action. The adjunction on module sheaves, with the actual abelian unit and counit, is [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-module-adjunction]. Here the pulled-back coefficient ring is the constant $A$, as in [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Thus [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] gives $p^*\dashv p_*$, $p'^*\dashv p'_*$ and $i^*\dashv i_*$, $i'^*\dashv i'_*$ on the derived categories, with termwise units and counits. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], exact direct images compute their right derived functors on $D^+$.

source.place: Stacks Tags 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero), 03DA (lemma-abelian), 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); exact adjunction localized termwise

proof.text: Use the right adjoints $i_*\dashv i^!$ and $i'_*\dashv i'^!$ supplied by [lem-exc-closed-ambient], denoting their units by $u,u'$ and counits by $e,e'$. They restrict to $D^+$. Indeed exactness makes $i_*$ and $i'_*$ preserve the standard classes $D^{\le n}$; if $M\in D^{\ge n}$ then $\operatorname{Hom}(T,i^!M)=\operatorname{Hom}(i_*T,M)=0$ for $T\in D^{\le n-1}$, so the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] gives $i^!M\in D^{\ge n}$. The same argument applies to $i'^!$. This uses only the ambient closed adjunction, with no constructibility, invertibility of the coefficient order, or exceptional adjoint for $p$.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 5.4.1, p. 291, paragraph applying i! to q_*K_{Y′} -> p_*K_{X′}; adjunction and counit calculation expanded by Q38

proof.text: The closed ordinary counit $i^*i_*N\to N$ is invertible on sheaves by [prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful]. It remains so for module sheaves: it is $A$-linear by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-module-adjunction], and the inverse of a bijective linear map is linear. By [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] it remains invertible termwise on derived categories. Now [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-counit-iso-right-fully-faithful] applied to $i^*\dashv i_*$ shows that the derived $i_*$ is fully faithful. Consequently the unit $u_N:N\to i^!i_*N$ is invertible: under $i_*\dashv i^!$, the map $\operatorname{Hom}(T,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,i^!i_*N)$ induced by $u_N$ is exactly the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(T,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}(i_*T,i_*N)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] to the opposite of $D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. We use $u^{-1}$ for the normalization $i^!i_*\cong1$.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 5.4.1, p. 291, paragraph applying i! to q_*K_{Y′} -> p_*K_{X′}; adjunction and counit calculation expanded by Q38

proof.text:
Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] to the square with finite direct-image map $i$ and base-change map $p$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $\theta_T:p^*i_*T\xrightarrow{\sim}i'_*p'^*T$. The map is $A$-linear: its defining restriction and adjunction maps in [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] are module-linear by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-module-adjunction]; an invertible linear map of abelian sheaves has linear inverse. Exactness from Step 2 allows the same termwise map on $D^+$. For $T\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $M\in D^+(X'_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ the ordinary and closed adjunctions therefore give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(T,p'_*i'^!M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(p'^*T,i'^!M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i'_*p'^*T,M)\xrightarrow{\circ\theta_T}\operatorname{Hom}(p^*i_*T,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_*T,p_*M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,i^!p_*M).$$
By [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] applied to the opposite category, these bijections are postcomposition with a unique isomorphism $\delta_M:p'_*i'^!M\xrightarrow{\sim}i^!p_*M$. Naturality of every bijection also gives naturality in $M$; the isomorphism requested in the statement is $\delta_M^{-1}$.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 5.4.1, p. 291, paragraph applying i! to q_*K_{Y′} -> p_*K_{X′}; adjunction and counit calculation expanded by Q38

proof.text:
We check the actual arrow. Write $a:p^*p_*\to1$ and $a':p'^*p'_*\to1$ for the ordinary counits. The definition of exchange in [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] gives
$$i'_*(a'_N)\circ\theta_{p'_*N}=a_{i'_*N}\circ p^*(c_N)$$
under the pullback-composition identifications. To verify this equality directly, transpose under $p^*\dashv p_*$ and evaluate on an etale $V\to X$: both maps restrict a section of $N$ on $V\times_XY'$ along the same projection, so give the identity of that section in $p_*i'_*N$. This uses the section formula of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and the linear adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-module-adjunction]. Put $N=i'^!M$. Tracing $1_{p'_*N}$ through the Hom bijections of Step 5 gives, on $X'$, the map
$$e'_M\circ i'_*(a'_N)\circ\theta_{p'_*N}=e'_M\circ a_{i'_*N}\circ p^*(c_N).$$
Naturality of $a$ changes the right side to $a_M\circ p^*(p_*e'_M\circ c_N)$. Its transpose under $p^*\dashv p_*$ is therefore $E_M=p_*e'_M\circ c_N:i_*p'_*N\to p_*M$, by the triangle identity. Its final transpose under $i_*\dashv i^!$ is
$$\delta_M=i^!(E_M)\circ u_{p'_*N}.$$
Thus $\delta$ is the comparison defined by the canonical exchange and ordinary adjunctions, with the prescribed closed counit, rather than an unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 5.4.1, p. 291, paragraph applying i! to q_*K_{Y′} -> p_*K_{X′}; adjunction and counit calculation expanded by Q38

proof.text:
Under $c_N$ the map in the statement is $i^!(E_M)$. By Step 6,
$$\delta_M^{-1}\circ i^!(E_M)\circ u_{p'_*i'^!M}=1_{p'_*i'^!M}.$$
Step 4 identifies its source $i^!i_*p'_*i'^!M$ with $p'_*i'^!M$ using $u^{-1}$, and Step 5 identifies its target with that same object using $\delta^{-1}$. Hence the specified map is the identity under precisely these identifications, and in particular is invertible. All computations are natural in $M$.
